page.seoHeadline: Share your screen online with a group, free
homeSeo.aboutBody1: Sharing your screen online is usually more hassle than it should be: download this, make an account there, schedule the meeting. Not here. You pick a name for a room, send the link, and whoever clicks it is already watching your screen in their browser. Free, no sign-up, and no timer cutting the call off halfway through.
homeSeo.aboutBody2: And it is not only your screen: turn on your camera, talk into your mic, type in the room's chat and see who has turned up. It works just as well for binge-watching a series with friends, gaming together or catching a stream as it does for showing your work to a study group or getting a quick meeting done without putting anything in anyone's calendar.
homeSeo.howToTitle: How to share your screen online in 3 steps
homeSeo.howToIntro: From nothing to the first person watching usually takes under a minute.
homeSeo.step1Title: Pick a name for the room
homeSeo.step1Body: Type it in the box up there and hit create. Make it public and it joins the list, so anyone can drop in. Make it private and you get a code, so only the people you invite can get in.
homeSeo.step2Title: Hit stream and choose what to show
homeSeo.step2Body: Your browser asks whether you want to share a tab, a window or the whole screen — and whether to send the audio along. Would rather show your face than your screen? Turn on the camera and mic. Or both at once, if you feel like it.
homeSeo.step3Title: Send the link to whoever is watching
homeSeo.step3Body: Paste it in the group chat and you are done. Anyone who clicks joins from the browser, on a computer or a phone, with nothing to install and no account to make. And anyone who shows up late drops straight into whatever is already happening.
homeSeo.featuresTitle: What you can do on GoLive
homeSeo.featureScreenBody: A tab, a window or the whole screen — sound included, exactly as you are hearing it.
homeSeo.featureCameraBody: Show up for the group whenever you want: just the camera, or the camera alongside your screen.
homeSeo.featureVoiceBody: The room doubles as a voice call, so you can chat away while everyone watches.
homeSeo.featurePrivateBody: Open for anyone to join, or locked with a code so it stays between you.
homeSeo.featureFreeTitle: Free, no sign-up, no closing time
homeSeo.featureFreeBody: Nothing to schedule and nobody gets kicked mid-conversation. Open it, make the room, that is it.
homeSeo.featureAppBody: The app captures system audio at better quality, and the bot spins up a room automatically in every call on your server.
homeSeo.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about screen sharing online
homeSeo.faq1Q: Is sharing your screen here really free?
homeSeo.faq1A: It is. Making a room, streaming your screen, camera and voice and watching along with everyone costs nothing, and there is no time limit per call. There is a GoLive Pro plan, which is optional and adds some extras — but everything written on this page works without it.
homeSeo.faq2Q: Do I have to install anything or make an account?
homeSeo.faq2A: No. Open the site, pick a room name and you can already share your screen. An account is optional and is what keeps your friends, groups and themes. If you want system audio coming through cleaner, that is when the desktop app is worth grabbing.
homeSeo.faq3Q: How many people can watch at once?
homeSeo.faq3A: A room is built for a group, not for a two-person call — plenty of people can be on the same stream. And anyone joining late picks up whatever is already happening, so nobody has to start over.
homeSeo.faq4Q: Can I share my screen with the audio too?
homeSeo.faq4A: You can. When you pick a tab or the whole screen, the browser offers to send the audio along, and in the desktop app it comes through better still. That is what saves the day when the plan is watching a video, listening to music or gaming together: nobody needs a second call just for the sound.
homeSeo.faq5Q: Does GoLive work on a phone?
homeSeo.faq5A: It does. From a phone browser you can watch, talk and stream your camera just fine. Sharing the phone's own screen depends on what that device's browser allows — Android usually does better at it.
homeSeo.faq6Q: Can anyone walk into my room?
homeSeo.faq6A: Only if you want them to. A public room shows up in the list and takes whoever arrives. A private room gets a code, appears in no list anywhere, and only lets in people holding the name and the code.
homeSeo.faq7Q: What is the difference from Zoom, Google Meet or Discord?
homeSeo.faq7A: Because the idea here is one thing only: throwing your screen, your camera and your voice to a group, in the browser, with nothing to install and nobody to sign up as. No meeting to schedule, no closing time, and the room's address is the name you picked.
